peer_results.rationale: The provided candidates for Bank of America (BAC) focus on regulatory capital stress testing (CCAR) and source of strength obligations. While CCAR involves economic scenarios, the disclosures describe regulatory capital requirements and buffer levels rather than the specific methodology for estimating expected credit losses (ECL) or the quantitative models (PD/LGD/EAD) and economic drivers (housing/unemployment) used for accounting ECL estimates as detailed in Citi's disclosure.

comparisons.peer_summary: Statements regarding expected provision for credit losses are subject to risk that actual losses may differ due to changes in loan portfolio composition, economic environment, forecasts, or management judgments and models.
comparisons.comparison: Both Citi and Goldman Sachs disclose that their expected credit loss provisions and estimates are sensitive to changes in the economic environment and management forecasts/models. Citi details the specific quantitative inputs (PD, LGD, EAD) and macro variables (housing, unemployment) used in its models to estimate expected credit losses. Similarly, Goldman Sachs highlights the risk that actual credit losses may differ from expectations due to changes in the economic environment, forecasts, and changes in their models and management judgments, indicating a shared reliance on forward-looking economic assessments for credit loss estimation.

sentences.text: The loss likelihood and severity models used for estimating expected credit losses are sensitive to changes in macroeconomic variables, including housing prices, unemployment rate and real GDP, and cover a wide range of geographic, industry, product and business segments.

Citi estimates expected credit losses for its quantitative component using (i) its comprehensive internal data on loss and default history, (ii) internal credit risk ratings, (iii) external credit bureau and rating agencies information and (iv) R&S forecasts of macroeconomic conditions.

Statements about our expected provision for credit losses are subject to the risk that actual credit losses may differ and our expectations may change, possibly materially, from that currently anticipated due to, among other things, changes to the composition of our loan portfolio and changes in the economic environment in future periods and our forecasts of future economic conditions, as well as changes in our models, policies and other management judgments.

peer_results.rationale: The provided candidates for JPMorgan Chase (JPM) relate to derivatives regulation in the EU and a general corporate overview. Neither disclosure addresses credit loss estimation methodology, economic variables impacting credit risk, or the quantitative components of expected credit losses.

The provided candidates for Morgan Stanley (MS) cover the location of financial data and general regulatory oversight including capital requirements under Basel III. These disclosures do not provide specific details on the methodology, models, or macroeconomic variables used to estimate expected credit losses comparable to Citi's quantitative component disclosure.
